patent.title: Patent Lab — Key Takeaways
points: A patent protects NEW INVENTIONS — new products or processes that solve a technical problem.
In India, a patent is valid for 20 years from the date of filing the application.
To be patentable, an invention must be Novel (new), involve an Inventive Step (non-obvious), and have Industrial Application (useful).
You cannot patent mathematical methods, scientific theories, plants/animals, or methods of agriculture in India.
Patents are granted by the Indian Patent Office (Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks).
A patent gives the inventor the exclusive right to make, use, sell or import the invention. Others need the inventor's permission (a licence).
patent.verify: All points based on the Patents Act, 1970 (as amended) — Sections 2, 3, 48, 53. Source: ipindia.gov.in

trademark.title: Trademark Tower — Key Takeaways
points: A trademark is a sign (word, logo, sound, colour, shape) that DISTINGUISHES the goods or services of one business from another.
A registered trademark in India is valid for 10 years and can be renewed indefinitely for further periods of 10 years each.
The ™ symbol means a mark is being used as a trademark (may not be registered). The ® symbol means it is officially REGISTERED.
Trademarks prevent consumer confusion — they help buyers know exactly whose product they are buying.
Using a fake or copied trademark (counterfeiting) is a criminal offence in India under the Trade Marks Act, 1999.
Well-known trademarks (like Tata, Amul) get extra protection even for goods and services they are not registered for.
trademark.verify: All points based on the Trade Marks Act, 1999 — Sections 2, 25, 28, 29, 103. Source: ipindia.gov.in

copyright.title: Copyright Cinema — Key Takeaways
points: Copyright protects ORIGINAL creative works — books, music, paintings, films, software, and more.
In India, copyright for literary, dramatic, musical and artistic works lasts for the author's LIFETIME plus 60 years.
Copyright protection is AUTOMATIC — you get it the moment you create an original work. Registration is optional but useful as evidence.
Fair dealing allows limited use of copyrighted works for education, research, criticism, news reporting, and personal/private use.
Piracy (copying and distributing copyrighted works without permission) is illegal and punishable under the Copyright Act, 1957.
The creator of a work has 'moral rights' — the right to be credited as the author and to prevent changes that harm their reputation.
copyright.verify: All points based on the Copyright Act, 1957 (as amended 2012) — Sections 13, 14, 17, 22, 52, 57. Source: copyright.gov.in

design.title: Design Studio — Key Takeaways
points: A registered design protects the VISUAL APPEARANCE of a product — its shape, pattern, ornamentation, or composition of colours.
Design registration does NOT protect how a product works (that is a patent) or the brand name on it (that is a trademark).
In India, a registered design is initially valid for 10 years, and can be extended by 5 more years (total 15 years).
To be registrable, a design must be new, original, and not previously published or disclosed to the public.
Design registration is especially important for industries like textiles, furniture, jewellery, toys, electronics and automobiles.
The Designs Act, 2000 governs design registration in India. Applications are filed with the Patent Office (Designs Wing).
design.verify: All points based on the Designs Act, 2000 — Sections 2, 4, 5, 11. Source: ipindia.gov.in
